title: Does the Best Plan Win
author: Hart, Nick
source: A Change is Gonna Come, April 11, 2026
summary: Based on Buckingham and Goodall's Nine Lies About Work, Hart argues schools over-emphasize detailed action plans that quickly become obsolete when faced with real complexity. Instead, successful teams need intelligence systems that move information rapidly so teams can react in real time. This requires trust in team members to make sense of data and clear communication of purpose over generic strategic documents.
points: Detailed action plans often become outdated quickly in complex school environments.
Intelligence systems that rapidly share current information are more useful than static strategic plans.
Teams need frequent access to reliable data so they can make responsive, timely decisions.
Regular check-ins on priorities matter more than written documentation of long-term plans.
Leadership teams must trust teachers to make good decisions when armed with accurate, current information.
quotes: Many plans, particularly those created in large organisations, are overly generalised, quickly obsolete and frustrating.
What great teams have is not a planning system, but an intelligence system.
Prioritise clarifying and communicating purpose over spending time writing action plans.
A team with low check in frequency is a team with low intelligence.
Decisions slow down. Similar situations are handled differently. Variation increases in ways that are not always productive.” Archived from A Change is Gonna Come on May 2, 2026 by Tim.
